topics.title: Diverse Perspectives on the State
topics.benchmark_preservation: The approved design reference, prior topic artifacts and canonical Political Theory owners remain immutable.

panels.panel_title: The State-Theory Problem and Its Stakes
lines: The State-Theory Problem and Its Stakes
[1] State theory asks about origin, purpose, liberty, inequality, society and change.
[2] Gauba compares competing images rather than announcing one final state doctrine.
[3] The state appears as ethical whole, instrument, class relation and group
[4] A theory becomes misleading when its partial insight is treated as exhaustive.
VERDICT -> State theory is plural because political power has several dimensions.
ANSWER USE -> Name the dimension before selecting or combining perspectives.
[1] Organic theory treats the state as natural; contract theory treats it as artificial.
[2] Laissez-faire limits the state, while welfare liberalism makes freedom enabling.
[3] Marxist, communitarian and post-colonial views relocate the source of political
[4] Gandhian, feminist and pluralist views challenge coercion, patriarchy and monopoly.
VERDICT -> Definitions locate each perspective before evaluation begins.
ANSWER USE -> Contrast the image of the state, not only the thinker's name.
[1] Origin asks whether the state is natural, contracted, class-produced or colonial.
[2] Purpose compares good life, rights, welfare, class rule, swaraj and coordination.
[3] Liberty ranges from obedience through non-interference to capacity and self-rule.
[4] Inequality, civil society and route to change complete the mandatory six-test grid.
VERDICT -> The six-test grid converts a list of theories into disciplined comparison.
ANSWER USE -> Apply the same dimensions to every perspective in the answer.
[1] Aristotle, Burke and Hegel develop natural, historical and ethical state images.
[2] Hobbes, Locke and Rousseau use contract for security, rights and popular
[3] Smith, Bentham, James Mill, Spencer and Nozick defend different limited-state
[4] J.S. Mill, Green, Hobhouse, Laski and MacIver revise liberalism toward welfare.
VERDICT -> Liberal traditions disagree internally about authority, rights and welfare.
ANSWER USE -> Separate contract, minimal-state and positive-liberal arguments.

panels.panel_title: Critical, Communitarian, Gandhian, Feminist and Pluralist Thinkers
lines: Critical, Communitarian, Gandhian, Feminist and Pluralist Thinkers

[2] Miliband argues instrumental capture; Poulantzas answers with bounded relative
[3] Communitarians stress embedded selves; post-colonial theory stresses inherited state
[4] Gandhi, Millett, Eisenstein and pluralists expose coercive, gendered and dispersed
VERDICT -> Critical theories differ over class, community, empire, coercion and gender.
ANSWER USE -> Use one internal debate before moving across traditions.
[1] Ten perspectives must be compared through the same six dimensions, not merely
[2] Organic and contract views prioritise ethical whole and authorised protection
[3] Minimal, welfare and Marxist views disagree about liberty, property and structural
[4] Communitarian, post-colonial, Gandhian, feminist and pluralist lenses widen the
VERDICT -> Each perspective illuminates one state function and obscures another.
ANSWER USE -> Compare attraction, mechanism and strongest limitation together.

panels.panel_title: Trap Repair, Boundaries, Revision and Sources
lines: Trap Repair, Boundaries, Revision and Sources
[1] Reject the claims that all contract theorists, liberals or feminist thinkers agree.
[2] Keep Miliband distinct from Poulantzas and Millett distinct from Eisenstein.
[3] Locke's text was largely composed before 1688 but later read as vindicating the
[4] Pluralism disperses power but does not prove equal groups or a neutral state.
VERDICT -> Precision depends on resisting false mergers and unsafe historical claims.
ANSWER USE -> Turn every common misconception into an explicit correction.

panels.panel_title: Theses, Directives and Marxist Argument Reconstruction
lines: Theses, Directives and Marxist Argument Reconstruction
[1] A rigorous thesis identifies which state image and which comparison dimension
[2] Directive control prevents liberalism, Marxism or feminism from being flattened.
[3] Miliband's personnel and leverage claim meets Poulantzas's structural-autonomy
[4] Relative autonomy remains bounded if the account is to retain a Marxist explanation.
VERDICT -> Relative autonomy explains mediation without making class power irrelevant.
ANSWER USE -> Present claim, objection and bounded reply in that order.
